summary:
Your forehand topspin is too upright: your knees are almost straight at contact (about 157°), so your arm does the work instead of your legs.

**What I made:** I found 18 rallies in your match, and the longest was 13 shots. The highlight reel holds the top 5 by shot count. I read your bat hand as right from the paddle colour across several rallies. Tell me if that's wrong.

**What to work on first:**
1. **Sit lower.** Your knee angle at contact is 157°. Fan Zhendong is at 114° and Ma Long at 126°. Aim for about 120-135° so your legs drive the brush up. At 30.8s your knees were at 135° and that was your best stroke.
2. **Hold a steady, wider base.** Your stance ranged from 1.36 to 2.74 shoulder widths, and it was 1.77 at the coached contact. Aim for about 2 shoulder widths every time. Your wide stance at 30.8s (2.74) went with your deepest knee bend. The narrow one at 54.6s (1.36) went with your straightest legs (166°).
3. **Start the bat lower.** Your bat arm is 13° higher at the backswing than Sun Yingsha's. Start below the ball so you can brush up, not hit down or flat.

**Keep:** your arm swings freely through the ball and finishes forward and across your body.

**Drill:** shadow swings in front of a mirror. Bend your knees to about 130°, drop the bat low, then brush up and finish with your knees still bent.

breakdown.headline: Sit Lower, Brush Up
breakdown.grip: Shakehand grip in your right hand; keep it loose and squeeze only at the ball.
breakdown.stance: Feet vary from 1.4 to 2.7 shoulder widths and your knees are almost straight (157°); settle at about 2 widths with deeper knees.
breakdown.swing_path: Your bat arm starts about 13° higher than Sun Yingsha's, so drop the bat low and swing from low to high.
breakdown.contact_point: You meet the ball in front with your wrist about midway between hip and shoulder; good, now add leg drive.
breakdown.follow_through: The arm finishes forward and across, but your legs are about 18° straighter than Ma Long's at the finish, so stay bent.

steps.title: DROP BAT LOW
lines: Bat starts below the ball, elbow close in.
Low start leaves room to brush up the ball.

steps.title: SIT LOWER
lines: Knees bent to about 120-135° at contact.
Legs drive the lift so the arm stays loose.

steps.title: STAY LOW
lines: Knees still bent as the bat ends high.
Standing up early costs spin and recovery.

breakdown.recap: Drop the bat low, sit into your legs at contact, and stay low as you finish.
breakdown.drill: Do 20 shadow forehands in front of a mirror: bend your knees to about 130°, start the bat low, brush up, and freeze at the finish with your knees still bent.
